episodes.196672: The interaction of Hurricane Kirk and another low pressure across the north Atlantic modulated the local weather pattern, pooling abundant moisture and promoting light winds in the region. Additionally, increasing instability due to the proximity of a mid to upper level trough favored deeper convection development each afternoon. This resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms each day along Puerto Rico, with daily amounts ranging from 2 to 4 inches, and localized higher amounts. With an elevated flooding risk, several flood and landslide reports were received.
episodes.197006: A quick moving shortwave passed across the area in the very early morning hours of October 4th. Despite modest available moisture fields, strong forcing and the deepening low were enough for convection to develop over central to eastern Iowa. Storms produced large amounts of pea sized hail in some locations with other areas reporting up to golf ball sized hail.
episodes.197470: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay area.
episodes.197575: A cold front with unseasonably warm air ahead of it  brought welcomed rainfall to portions of southeast Iowa (where pockets of 0.5 to over 1 were observed. A few of these storms were marginally severe with hail around 1 inch.
episodes.197577: A cold front with unseasonably warm air ahead of it brought  a marginally severe storm with hail to far northeast Missouri during the early morning hours of October 4th.
